releases.name: v0.3.2 — Native Agent Plugins & OpenCode V2
releases.body:
Native memory packages for supported agent harnesses, with an OpenCode V2 adapter and evidence-aware memory operations.

## Native agent plugins
- Luminary-maintained packages for OpenCode, pi, and omp, built from the same canonical adapters as the Python hook installer.
- Native memory tools and accurate stored, duplicate, skipped, error, and deletion results.
- pi and omp expose `/luminary` commands and native terminal interactions; compatible clients can consume their serialized results.

## OpenCode V2
- Targets `@opencode/cli` 2.1.4 and `@opencode/plugin` 2.1.4 with `Plugin.define`, Promise domain APIs, and the plural `plugins` configuration.
- Automatic recall reads the admitted native user message; optional curation runs after successful execution.
- Session-owned workspace resolution prevents one shared plugin instance from reading another workspace.
- The older npm `0.3.1` adapter remains the V1 target; the V1 Ecosystem submission pins that exact version.

## Memory ownership and accuracy
- Shared UTF-8 JSON bridge enforces user, workspace, and harness ownership.
- Explicit remember and ID-scoped forget use real storage outcomes, not inferred success.
- Automatic durable writes require opt-in LLM curation grounded in the user message; assistant-only claims are rejected.
- Telegram activity uses destination-specific cursors and evidence-bearing results rather than attributing global new IDs to the current turn.

## Installation and downloads
Install the Python bridge from PyPI:

```sh
python -m pip install --upgrade luminary-memory==0.3.2
```

The release assets contain compiled `0.3.2` plugin tarballs for OpenCode, pi, and omp, plus the Hermes skill zip. All three npm packages are published at `0.3.2`, with `latest` pointing to that version: `luminary-memory-opencode`, `luminary-memory-pi`, and `luminary-memory-omp`. Their registry SHA-512 checksums match the release assets.

## Verification
- Python 3.11/3.12, PostgreSQL integration, and native-package CI passed before the source merge.
- The real default embedding-model release gate passed before PyPI publication.
- The published npm OpenCode `0.3.2` package was installed through the real V2 CLI, loaded as an active package plugin in server `2.1.4`, and stored a fact through the published PyPI wheel.
- Real OpenCode V2 native sessions, Python, and SQLite exercised scoped memory operations, automatic recall, grounded curation, rejection of assistant-only claims, and cleanup on plugin removal. Model/curation replies used deterministic localhost fixtures; this is not a model-quality benchmark or a desktop/web visual test.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/alertxsto/luminary-memory/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

releases.name: v0.3.0 — Memory Accuracy & Session Continuity
releases.body:
Major release: memory is now scoped, evidenced, and auditable end to end.

## Scope isolation
- New `scope` module centralizes tenant/scope SQL predicates used by every recall path (SQLite, pgvector, graph, keyword, temporal)
- Legacy/global rows stay visible to scoped callers through a compatibility mode

## Schema and storage
- New tables: `episodes`, `claims`, `claim_evidence`, `memory_evidence`, `memory_events`
- Cross-process active dedup via scoped unique content-hash constraint
- SQLite schema now evolves existing databases, not just fresh installs

## Claims and evidence
- Structured claims with grounded evidence quotes, canonical keys, and full lifecycle (active, superseded, retracted)
- Evidence fail-closed in every recall mode: fabricated quotes cannot become answer support

## Hermes provider
- Every accepted turn enters a per-session episode ledger before curation
- When durable recall abstains, recent exact-session episodes are injected as bounded untrusted reference (active-task continuity)
- Serialized post-turn reconciliation can capture a new grounded fact or supersede/retract a scoped claim
- Scoped JSONL transparency events without prompt content or credentials

## Enricher
- Transport switched from `urllib` to `requests`; `urllib` is blocked by Cloudflare (HTTP 1010) on OpenAI-compatible gateways
- Failures surface as `enricher_failed` events instead of being swallowed into `llm_no_curated_summary`

## Lifecycle and maintenance
- Cleanup, prune, consolidate, and runner hardening
- Authority repair utility with dry-run and backup before apply
- Telegram activity hook requires the `ok` envelope and retries failures

## Docs and website
- Guides refreshed for the new surfaces; website content and styles rebuilt

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/alertxsto/luminary-memory/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
